Sunny afternoon, a dusty small-town baseball field in Cedar Hollow, wooden bleachers full of villagers, an American flag on a pole.
0–3s: Kid Frost holds a wooden baseball bat that looks like a toothpick in his huge hands.

DIALOGUE 7–10s: Frost (deep young heroic voice): "Home Run is where I stand for my family."
DIALOGUE 10–12s: Hank (rough kind villager voice): "We fix what Home Run broke before dark."
12–22s: Quick comedic cut: the crowd still looking up, eating popcorn. Martha falls asleep. A dog lies down. The sun moves across the sky.
DIALOGUE 17–20s: Tommy (young excited man): "Tell me someone else saw Home Run."
22–30s: The ball finally falls from the sky and lands right in Frost's hand. The crowd goes wild.
DIALOGUE 25–30s: Tommy (young excited man): "I saw Home Run with my own eyes."
Final frame: villagers lifting Frost (with a lot of effort) and cheering.
SFX: bat crack, whistle of the ball flying away, crickets, popcorn crunching, snoring, falling whistle, catch thump, cheering crowd.
MUSIC: classic American ballpark organ tune, then triumphant brass.
